header.title: Your Exercise Program
header.subtitle: Follow your daily routine to support knee recovery.

quadSets.name: Quad Sets
quadSets.description: Strengthens the quadriceps to support knee stability.
instructions: Sit or lie down with the leg supported and the knee straight.
Tighten the front of the thigh, as if pressing the knee down.
Hold the contraction briefly.
Relax slowly and repeat.
cues: Keep the movement controlled, not forceful.
Stop if you feel sharp pain.

legRaises.name: Straight Leg Raises
legRaises.description: Improves thigh control and reduces knee pressure.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg straight.
Tighten the thigh of the straight leg.
Lift it slowly to the height of the bent knee.
Lower it back down with control.
cues: Keep the knee straight throughout the lift.
Move slowly rather than swinging the leg.
Keep your lower back relaxed against the surface.
mistakes: Letting the knee bend during the lift.
Lifting too high or too fast.

heelSlides.name: Heel Slides
heelSlides.description: Enhances knee flexion and mobility safely.
instructions: Lie on your back with legs straight.
Slowly slide your heel toward your body, bending the knee.
Go as far as comfortable, then pause.
Slide the heel back to the starting position.
cues: Keep the movement smooth and slow.
Stop at the first sign of sharp pain.
Support the movement with your hands if needed.
mistakes: Forcing the knee further than comfortable.
Letting the foot lift off the surface.

hamstring.name: Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit with the leg extended in front of you.
Keep your back straight and gently lean forward from the hips.
Hold the stretch without bouncing.
Release slowly.
cues: Stretch until you feel gentle tension, not pain.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
mistakes: Rounding the back to reach further.

calfRaises.name: Calf Raises
calfRaises.description: Strengthens lower leg muscles for stability.
instructions: Stand with your feet flat, holding support if needed.
Slowly rise onto your toes.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower back down with control.
cues: Keep the movement slow and controlled.
Distribute weight evenly across both feet.
Use support for balance if needed.

cards.exercisesDescription: Patients leave the clinic with a printed sheet and no way to track whether they actually followed it.
cards.painDescription: A five-minute visit rarely captures how pain and mobility really changed week to week.
cards.decisionsDescription: Without daily data, clinicians adjust treatment plans on memory instead of evidence.

physicalTherapy.question: Is KneeGuide a replacement for physical therapy?
physicalTherapy.answer: No. KneeGuide is designed to complement your care team's treatment plan by keeping them informed between visits, not to replace clinical guidance.

doctorVisibility.question: How does my doctor see my daily logs?
doctorVisibility.answer: Everything you log — pain levels, mobility and exercises — syncs to your care team's dashboard in real time.

dataSecurity.question: Is my health data secure?
dataSecurity.answer: Yes. All data is encrypted end-to-end and handled to clinical-grade privacy standards.

equipment.question: Do I need special equipment to use KneeGuide?
equipment.answer: No. Just your phone or a browser. The 3D model and tracking tools run directly, with no extra hardware required.

noReferral.question: Can I use KneeGuide without a referring doctor?
noReferral.answer: Yes. You can create a patient account directly. Connecting with a clinician is optional, though recommended for the full experience.
